[عدل | عدل المصدر]
كلية الزراعة هي أول كلية زراعة في العراق، يعود تاريخ تأسيسها إلى عام 1952. تتوزع بناياتها وحقولها على مساحة 400 دونم، منها 100 دونم تنتشر عليها بنايات العمادة والأقسام العلمية والمكتبة والقاعات والمختبرات الدراسية والورش والمعامل و300 دونم حقول وبساتين مخصصه لتدريب الطلبة ولإجراء بحوث وتجارب الاساتذه وطلبة الدراسات العليا. ومدة الدراسة للحصول على شهادة الماجستير سنتان وللحصول على شهادة الدكتوراه ثلاث سنوات وفق نظام الكورسات والبحث العلمي.[1]

value.text:
The College of Agricultural Engineering Sciences (كلية علوم الهندسة الزراعية) is a constituent college of the University of Baghdad in Iraq. Located in Al-Jadriya, it traces its establishment to 1952 and is also described under the name College of Agriculture (كلية الزراعة). Its work combines agricultural education with practical training and research in fields and laboratories. The college offers undergraduate and postgraduate education in agricultural disciplines.

The bachelor’s programme in agricultural sciences is described as a four-year course organised into two semesters per academic year. Postgraduate study developed through individual departments: master’s study began in plant protection in 1961, while doctoral study was introduced in field crops in 1975. The historical account describes master’s programmes lasting two years and doctoral programmes lasting three years, combining coursework with research.

Its academic areas include animal production, food science and biotechnology, horticulture and garden engineering, plant protection, soil and water sciences, agricultural machinery, field crops, agricultural economics, and agricultural extension. The animal-production department dates to the college’s foundation in 1952. Teaching and training facilities described in the institutional history include scientific departments, a library, classrooms, laboratories, workshops, agricultural fields and orchards used for student training and postgraduate research.

The College of Agricultural Engineering Sciences (كلية علوم الهندسة الزراعية) is a constituent college of the University of Baghdad in Iraq. Located in Al-Jadriya, it traces its establishment to 1952 and is also described under the name College of Agriculture (كلية الزراعة). Its work combines agricultural education with practical training and research in fields and laboratories. The college offers undergraduate and postgraduate education in agricultural disciplines.

The bachelor’s programme in agricultural sciences is described as a four-year course organised into two semesters per academic year. Postgraduate study developed through individual departments: master’s study began in plant protection in 1961, while doctoral study was introduced in field crops in 1975. The historical account describes master’s programmes lasting two years and doctoral programmes lasting three years, combining coursework with research.

Its academic areas include animal production, food science and biotechnology, horticulture and garden engineering, plant protection, soil and water sciences, agricultural machinery, field crops, agricultural economics, and agricultural extension. The animal-production department dates to the college’s foundation in 1952. Teaching and training facilities described in the institutional history include scientific departments, a library, classrooms, laboratories, workshops, agricultural fields and orchards used for student training and postgraduate research.
